To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perceived risks, trust, product involvement and perceived usefulness are the main factors influencing internet banking services adoption.

(1) the perceived risks (security and performance risks, privacy risk and social risk) are the key factors in internet banking use; (2) trust reduces perceived risk; and (3) product involvement has a direct impact on perceived ease of use.
trust, perceived risk, product involvement and technology acceptance model beliefs have a positive impact on internet banking services adoption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of trust and risk dimensions on internet banking adoption and the role of product (financial service) involvement.
the role of trust, perceived risk and product involvement in the adoption of internet banking.
identifying the determinants of e-banking adoption in the context of a developing country, where there are still few studies on the subject.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of online banking is determined by perceived usefulness and ease of use, trust and risk dimensions.
trust, perceived risk, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and product involvement are important determinants of internet bank adoption.

perceived security, privacy, performance, and social risk have a significant and negative effect on the intention to use e-banking services, while trust has a positive and significant influence on the intention to adopt e-banking services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the more the user trusts the bank, the lower the perceived risks and the greater the perceived usefulness and ease of use of internet banking services, and therefore the greater the adoption rate of internet banking services.
trust and perceived risks are important antecedents of internet banking adoption and that perceived risk can be reduced by increasing perceived ease of usefulness.
trust and perceived risks are key drivers for internet banking services adoption, while product involvement and perceived ease of use are key determinants of perceived usefulness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
perceived risk dimensions have a significant impact on the adoption of internet banking services.
trust plays an important role for reducing perceived risks, which in turn increase the adoption of internet banking services.
trust is the most important variable in reducing perceived risk, and perceived risk is a significant determinant of internet banking adoption.
